title: Paste-and-go, zero-question agent prompts (self-install, never interrogate)
detail: An agent prompt that self-installs its CLI silently, streams if the key is present, and carries on quietly if not — never stopping to ask the user.
why: Interrogation kills the 'automatic' feel. One-time machine setup + paste-and-go everywhere is what made Bug Ledger feel effortless.
how: Serve the CLI from a public URL so it installs with a single curl; read the key from a small key file (no shell-profile dependency); tell the agent to self-heal silently and NEVER 'stop and ask' when something is missing.

title: One-shot entrance animations (never re-animate on refresh)
detail: Put entrance animations on a one-shot class that is stripped after it plays, not on the base element.
why: Moving or re-inserting a DOM node restarts its CSS animation — so a live board re-fades every poll and 'blinks every second'.
how: .card.enter{animation} then removeClass after ~600ms; and only touch the DOM order when the sorted order actually changed.

title: In-place DOM updates for live views (diff, don't re-render)
detail: Update existing nodes field-by-field each poll and animate only what changed, instead of rewriting innerHTML.
why: Wholesale re-render flickers, drops scroll/focus, and replays animations.
how: Keep a refs map per card; compare to last state; mutate only changed text/classes; add a transient 'pop' class on the item that just completed.

title: Aurora-glass design language
detail: Soft near-white canvas + slowly drifting aurora gradient blobs + frosted-glass cards + a single warm accent (coral) + big rounded type.
why: Reads as premium and high-end, and keeps every app in the portfolio visually coherent.
how: A fixed, blurred aurora layer of 3–4 radial-gradient blobs with a slow drift keyframe; cards use rgba white + backdrop-filter blur + hairline border + soft shadow.

title: Theme-aware from the first line
detail: Design light and dark together with CSS variables and prefers-color-scheme, not as an afterthought.
why: Respects the viewer's system and avoids a jarring bright flash in dark environments.
how: :root design tokens + a single @media (prefers-color-scheme: dark) override block; test both before shipping.

title: Live progress counter for long tasks (N / total)
detail: Stream a running 'checked N / total' counter for long agent work so the user sees exactly where it reached.
why: Transparency and watchability build trust; a silent long task feels stuck.
how: Carry progress {done,total,label} on the session; update it every step; show it as a big number + a bar on a live board.

title: Empty states as first-class design
detail: Design the 'nothing here yet' state beautifully with a clear next action, not a blank page.
why: First impressions and guidance — most people see the empty state first.
how: A calm, centered message on the same aurora background, naming the exact command/step that will fill it.

title: Full date + timestamp on records (not just relative time)
detail: Show the full date and time to the second on activity and audit entries.
why: Auditability — 'when exactly did this run?' matters for a record.
how: Format as 'DD Mon YYYY, HH:MM:SS'; keep relative time only for the currently-live item.

title: Server-verified completeness, not self-report
detail: When an agent claims it checked everything, verify it server-side and show N/N plus the exact items missed.
why: Proof beats assurance; it stops silent skipping.
how: Match the agent's reported titles against the catalog on the server; return {matched,total,missed}; loop until complete.

title: Append-only records (add, never modify or delete)
detail: Make the durable record add-only at the database level so agents can contribute but never corrupt or delete.
why: Safe multi-agent contribution and a trustworthy audit trail.
how: SQLite BEFORE UPDATE/DELETE triggers that RAISE(ABORT); a documented owner-only escape hatch for pruning.

title: Never cache a failure
detail: Only cache a successful, non-empty fetch; caching a transient failure poisons the isolate until redeploy.
why: One bad checklist fetch once silently returned 0/0 coverage for everyone on that isolate.
how: Guard the cache assignment on a non-empty result; on failure return a fallback WITHOUT storing it.

title: Keep source NUL-free
detail: Never embed a literal NUL (0x00) in source — e.g. as a cache-key delimiter.
why: It makes grep/file treat the whole file as binary and silently match nothing, so agents wrongly conclude the code is missing.
how: Use the \u0000 escape or a printable delimiter; grep -a as a fallback when a file mysteriously matches nothing.

title: Network-first HTML in service workers
detail: Serve navigations network-first (or bump the cache name every deploy) so shipped fixes aren't masked by a stale cached shell.
why: Cache-first service workers pin returning users to an old build — a bug that recurred across many apps.
how: Network-first fetch handler for document requests; version the cache name on each release.

title: Version-stamp assets (?v=) every deploy
detail: Append a ?v=N stamp to local script/style URLs each deploy so browsers can't serve stale JS/CSS.
why: Stale-CSS/JS bugs where a fix ships but the browser keeps the old file.
how: Bump ?v= on every deploy (or hash the asset).

title: Grounded AI that never invents
detail: Constrain the assistant to page/transcript context only, with a local fallback, and forbid fabrication.
why: Trust — a made-up fact or call detail is worse than 'I don't know'.
how: System prompt: answer only from provided context, never invent; local FAQ/summary fallback when the model is unavailable.

title: Source-verified stats only (ban folklore)
detail: Only show a statistic you can cite to a primary source; ban unsourced 'best practice' numbers.
why: Credibility — one bogus stat undermines the whole product.
how: Keep a small vetted stats bank; no number ships without a citation.

title: Premium inputs & micro-interactions (no native dialogs)
detail: Replace native prompt()/alert()/confirm() with in-app modals; add smooth press states, hairline borders, subtle fills.
why: Native browser dialogs look broken and cheap; micro-polish signals quality.
how: Custom modal/toast components; :active transitions; consistent radius and spacing tokens.

title: Confirm-first for destructive or outward actions
detail: Deletes, sends, and voice/agent commands confirm before acting.
why: Prevents irreversible mistakes and builds trust in automation.
how: A confirm step (or undo window) before any send/delete; never auto-fire outward actions.

title: Balanced editorial layout — no orphaned whitespace
detail: Structure a section as a full-width strip + an aligned card grid so rows line up and nothing is left 'stranded' in one column.
why: 'Left over, not placed' whitespace is exactly what reads as unfinished/cheap.
how: Full-bleed gallery strip (6→3→2 across) then a 2×2 grid (About·Testimonials / FAQ·Policies); a full-bleed strip becomes its own fold.

title: Editorial typography: serif display + tabular numerals
detail: Serif display headlines, ledger/tabular numerals, caps-tracked labels, intentional whitespace, layered depth (soft shadow + blur), restraint over flash.
why: This is the consensus 2026 'premium' ingredient list; it reads as considered and expensive.
how: Serif for headings/commerce, tabular-nums for figures, 2-line clamps on overlays; restraint, not more effects.

title: Glassmorphism with restraint (floating chrome only)
detail: Use frosted glass selectively — on floating chrome (modals, aha hero), not on every surface.
why: Glass everywhere muddies legibility and stops reading premium; restraint is the premium signal.
how: A dedicated .glass class for floating elements; opaque premium cards elsewhere.

title: Premium SVG icons instead of emoji in chrome
detail: Replace bright emoji in nav/tools/buttons with a coherent inline-SVG icon set.
why: Emoji-as-chrome reads amateur; a stroke-consistent icon set reads like a real product.
how: Inline SVG, ~1.6 stroke, currentColor so icons inherit theme; one consistent set across the app.

title: Real editorial imagery, never stock people
detail: Bundle a small in-house image library (no people, no text, one soft-light style) and hide any tile whose image fails.
why: Stock-people photos make apps generic; a broken image is worse than none.
how: Generate/curate a few consistent images; a broken-image fallback that hides the tile so a 404 never shows.

title: Bento hierarchy + gradient washes + real photography
detail: Compose with a bento grid, gentle gradient washes and genuine subject photography for a high-end look.
why: This is the '$100k look' — clear hierarchy and real texture instead of flat boxes.
how: Bento tiles with varied sizes, soft gradient backgrounds, real photos over placeholder blocks.

title: Frosted-glass device bezel for previews
detail: Frame a live preview in a translucent glass device edge, not a thick black slab.
why: The black bezel looks like a placeholder; frosted glass looks designed.
how: Translucent edge + soft highlight/shadow + subtle notch + a 'LIVE PREVIEW' caption.

title: Layout diversity by content type
detail: Give different content modes genuinely different anatomies, not one template recolored.
why: Two prompts should produce two visibly different products; sameness reads as a wrapper.
how: Editorial = quiet grouped rows + stat strip (no hero); imagery-led = photo card grid; commerce = its own.

title: Shareable summary cards that market the app
detail: Generate a beautiful downloadable month/year card with kind, encouraging analysis and the app URL in the footer.
why: It delights the user and markets the app every time it's shared.
how: Canvas card: colour ribbon, stat tiles, one warm encouraging line, app URL footer.

title: Uniform pill pickers (avoid flex:1 ballooning)
detail: Make a format/segmented picker natural-width uniform pills, not flex:1 chips.
why: flex:1 makes buttons stretch and the last wrap-row balloon — visibly broken.
how: Non-stretching pills, uniform height, one icon each, a single accent on the selected one.

title: Onboarding: 1–2 fields per screen
detail: Ask one or two fields per onboarding screen, never a wall of inputs.
why: The first session is where 70–90% of users are lost; density kills completion.
how: One question per step; progressive disclosure; the PIN/passcode can double as a later lock code.

title: Endowed-progress onboarding
detail: Show the user already partway along the onboarding path rather than starting at zero.
why: Endowed progress lifts completion (34% vs 19%, Nunes & Drèze) and time-to-value under 5 min drives activation.
how: Pre-fill/first-step-done state; a progress indicator that starts a notch in.

title: Blank start + explorable demo (kept separate)
detail: New users land in their own empty workspace; a rich demo is a separate, clearly-labelled choice.
why: Mixing demo data into a real account confuses ownership and pollutes the user's space.
how: 'Start my own' → empty studio; 'Explore a demo' loads seeded data in a distinct mode.

title: One-tap row actions; confirm routine, danger card destructive
detail: Each row gets one-tap actions; routine actions show a small confirm, destructive ones a distinct danger card that never auto-runs.
why: Speed for the common case, a deliberate stop for the irreversible one.
how: Danger card for cancel/delete with a match picker when several items fit; never auto-execute.

title: 'New since last visit' + repeat-client cues
detail: Badge items that arrived since the last visit and flag returning clients.
why: Reviewers explicitly want at-a-glance 'what's new' and client history one tap away.
how: 'New' badges keyed to last-seen timestamp; '2nd visit' chips + one-tap client notes.

title: Honest labor steps instead of spinners
detail: Show the real named steps of a long operation instead of an opaque spinner.
why: Itemised 'labour' feels faster and more trustworthy than a mystery spinner.
how: Render each step as it runs ('reading transcript… drafting… saving'), not a single loader.

title: Auto-update bar — never run a stale build
detail: Any open tab checks for a newer deploy and offers a one-tap refresh.
why: Users otherwise sit on an old bundle after you ship a fix.
how: On focus/interval, compare a build stamp; show a 'Refresh' bar when a newer one is live.

title: Cancel symmetry (FTC click-to-cancel)
detail: Let users cancel in the same sheet where they signed up, effective at period end.
why: It's the FTC click-to-cancel standard and it builds trust; asymmetric cancellation feels like a trap.
how: One-tap cancel in the upgrade/billing sheet; confirm effective-at-period-end.

title: Streaks with mercy (never shame)
detail: Reward streaks but never shame a miss.
why: The 'abstinence-violation effect' makes people rage-quit after one slip.
how: Forgiving streaks/grace days; encouraging copy on a miss, never punitive.

title: Reduced-motion + aria-labels on icon buttons
detail: Honor prefers-reduced-motion and label every icon-only button.
why: Accessibility and polish; motion-sensitive users and screen readers both need it.
how: @media (prefers-reduced-motion) to cut animation; aria-label on each icon button.

title: Replace fabricated metrics with honest editable badges
detail: Never ship invented performance numbers; use honest, editable placeholders.
why: Fake '0.38s load / top 1% conversion' metrics destroy trust the moment they're noticed.
how: Editable badge components with truthful defaults; no unverifiable claims baked in.

title: Restraint as the premium signal
detail: State value with restraint ('plans are simply the better rate') instead of pushy gating.
why: Understatement itself reads premium; hard-sell reads cheap.
how: Calm, factual value copy; no dark-pattern nudges or fear-based gating.

title: Stage only the files you touched (concurrent-session safety)
detail: When another session may be editing the same repo, commit file-by-file, only the files you changed.
why: A blanket 'git add -A' sweeps a parallel agent's in-progress work into your commit.
how: git add specific paths; verify HEAD/diff before committing when co-editing.

title: Crash-recovery must never wipe user content
detail: A self-heal/crash-recovery path may purge caches and the service worker, never user data.
why: A recovery that clears storage can destroy the user's content — a worse failure than the crash.
how: Scope resets to SW + caches only; keep user data untouched; audit every self-heal path.

title: Write a world-class mandate + house rules into the repo
detail: Put the quality bar and build conventions in a repo doc every future feature must meet.
why: It keeps standards from drifting across sessions and agents.
how: A BUILD.md standing rule (editable-everything, delete-confirm, glass, timestamps, local-first, both themes, verified in-browser).

title: Deep-research with counter-evidence before design decisions
detail: Research a design/product decision against sources AND actively seek counter-evidence before committing.
why: Trend-following without counter-evidence ships generic or wrong choices (e.g. 'is glassmorphism still premium in 2026?').
how: A short research pass that cites sources and the case against; then decide.

title: Marketing landing at root, app at /app
detail: Serve a marketing landing at the root and the app at /app; returning users skip the landing.
why: New visitors get a pitch; existing users aren't slowed by it.
how: Root = landing; /app = product; redirect onboarded users straight to /app.

title: Never flatten a signature boot/splash animation
detail: Keep a signature animated splash (e.g. rainbow aurora) animated — don't 'optimize' it to a static image.
why: The boot moment is a brand signature; making it static quietly cheapens the whole app.
how: Preserve the keyframes; respect prefers-reduced-motion instead of removing it.

title: Re-audit security after every AI iteration
detail: Run a security pass after each round of AI edits, not just at the end.
why: Iterative AI generation measurably degrades security — each edit can re-introduce flaws.
how: A /securitysweep (or quick detector pass) after each significant AI change; treat 'it worked' as separate from 'it's safe'.

title: Treat all model output as untrusted
detail: Validate and sanitize anything an LLM returns before rendering, running or forwarding it.
why: LLM output can carry XSS/SSRF/command payloads (OWASP: improper output handling).
how: Encode before HTML, allow-list before navigation/exec, schema-validate structured output.

title: Least-privilege + human-in-the-loop for AI agents
detail: Give AI features only the tools/permissions they need and require approval for irreversible/outward actions.
why: Excessive agency is an exploitable attack surface (OWASP LLM).
how: Scope tokens/tools per task; confirm before send/delete/purchase; log agent actions.

title: Parameterize everything, escape on output
detail: Never build queries or markup by string-concatenating input; parameterize queries and encode at the output sink.
why: The two most common AI-code flaws are missing sanitization and XSS.
how: Prepared statements for data; an esc() that handles quotes + CSP for HTML.

title: OAuth token never touches the browser — server-side exchange + proxied API calls
detail: For third-party sign-in, the Worker swaps the OAuth code for a token using the client secret, stores it server-side per user, and proxies every API call so the page reads private data without holding a credential
why: A leaked client-held token exposes the user's private third-party data; server-side + proxy makes leakage structurally impossible
how: Worker routes /oauth/start and /oauth/callback (secret in env), a tokens table, and /api/<provider>/* proxy endpoints gated by the session cookie; browser only calls your own proxy

title: Device-link key provisioning (no secret pasted into chat/transcript)
detail: When an agent CLI has no key, it prints a short Approve link; the signed-in user clicks Approve once and the CLI polls, self-provisions its key to a local file, and starts streaming
why: Pasting a raw key into an agent chat leaves the secret in the transcript; a one-click device link is easier and safer
how: A device_codes table, a public /link/<code> approval page (401->sign-in-first guard), start/poll endpoints, and a cookie-authed approve; the CLI polls until approved then writes the key locally

title: CLIs must fail loudly, never silently no-op
detail: A served/worklog CLI that silently succeeded on a missing key or unknown verb misled users and agents into thinking work was recorded when nothing happened
why: Silent success hides breakage and sends agents down wrong paths (rebuilding clients, 'no key' with no guidance)
how: Exit non-zero with a clear message on missing key/unknown command; point the user to the recovery command (login/connect)

title: Scope CLI/tool state per-repo, never a shared global config path
detail: A worklog CLI wrote per-run state to cwd/.aprizely.json, which collided with the global token file at ~/.aprizely.json when run from home — clobbering the auth token
why: A shared or ambiguous state path silently overwrites config/tokens and clobbers other projects' runs
how: Write per-run state to a distinctly-named, cwd-scoped file, refuse to read a worklog file as config, and gitignore it

title: Always re-fetch a served CLI each run — 'install only if missing' goes stale
detail: A prompt that only re-installed the CLI when the file was absent left agents running an outdated cached copy lacking newer commands, so it printed 'No key' forever
why: Because the CLI is served (not versioned in a clone), any server-side change needs a re-fetch or clients silently run old code
how: Make the setup step always curl the latest CLI (overwrite), and add an explicit login/connect fallback for parity

title: Defensive per-item rendering so one bad record can't blank a whole view
detail: A single malformed record (a string where an array was expected) threw and blanked an entire list view
why: Lists that render items in one unguarded pass are fragile — one corrupt row takes down everything
how: Wrap/guard each item's render independently so a bad record degrades to a skipped/placeholder entry instead of aborting the list

title: Dependency-free client-side CSV + PDF export
detail: Spreadsheet/table data exported to a real .csv (proper quoting) and a genuine .pdf via a ~90-line dependency-free PDF generator
why: Reusable export without pulling heavy libraries; keeps bundles small and works offline in the browser
how: Build the PDF bytes by hand and validate the xref offsets point to real objects so any viewer accepts the file; verify CSV quoting on values with commas/quotes

title: User-customizable data grid (reorder, resize, persisted, delete-confirm)
detail: A spreadsheet view where users drag to reorder columns, drag borders to resize, edit cells inline, and delete rows with a confirm — layout persisted per user
why: Turns a static table into an Airtable/Excel-grade tool people can shape to their own workflow
how: Layout-driven column model with a colgroup, drag handles on headers, resize handles on borders, width/order saved per-user, native confirm on row delete

title: Self-healing demo isolation via a fixed demo fingerprint
detail: Detect demo data that leaked into a real account (known ids/nickname) and reset it to a clean state on load, while keeping the landing demo fully intact
why: Explorable demos routinely bleed into new accounts; a fingerprint-based auto-heal fixes already-polluted accounts without manual cleanup
how: On cloudPull, if state matches the demo fingerprint, reset to a fresh blank state; also reset on signup before adopting the account

title: Honest usage analytics — predict from user snapshots, never scrape or invent
detail: A usage/credits view with burn-rate and upgrade-runway predictions grounded only in user-logged (or agent-posted) snapshots plus the tier multiplier the plan panel already shows
why: No API exposes subscription usage, so scraping/guessing would fabricate numbers; logging snapshots keeps analytics truthful
how: Ingest usage snapshots via a keyed endpoint or manual entry; compute burn-rate/projection from history and base upgrade math only on the known tier multiplier

title: Click-to-understand plain-English step notes for agent actions
detail: Each agent-logged task/step carries a one-line description of what it does, why, and its effect; users tap a step to read it
why: Non-technical users can follow exactly what an agent is doing without reading code or jargon
how: CLI accepts Task::description in --tasks and a --desc flag on step/done; the live board, report timeline, and activity items expose an expandable info affordance

title: Show-but-lock gated features instead of hiding them
detail: Premium (Business-tier) rooms stay visible to every user with a lock badge in the nav/menu; clicking opens an upgrade wall rather than the feature
why: Hidden features can't sell themselves — showing the locked feature lets users see exactly what they'd gain
how: One BIZ_VIEWS set drives three gates consistently: nav lock badge, mobile-menu lock, and a render-level upgradeWall on the view

title: Per-plan AI usage quotas to protect margin
detail: Monthly AI call quotas metered in D1 per plan (vision counts triple; anonymous capped by IP)
why: Uncapped AI features can be abused and erode margin; per-plan caps keep high gross margin while staying generous
how: Mirror the existing TTS quota pattern in the worker; on cap-hit fall back to an on-device result plus a gentle upgrade nudge

title: In-app device-framed live preview of the real public page
detail: A booking Overview tab shows the actual public booking page rendered inside a phone/desktop frame (with a device toggle + QR), driven by the real template and the user's current data
why: Users otherwise never see their public-facing page without publishing and opening it in a new tab
how: Render the same public template with current state into an iframe/frame; add a device-size toggle and reuse the existing QR helper

title: Graceful filler imagery that vanishes on real upload
detail: Cover, portrait, service thumbnails and a photo gallery fall back to tasteful stock images (seeded by the page slug so they stay stable) and adapt to fewer photos than the demo; fully editable
why: Empty grey image boxes read as broken; stable placeholders keep the preview presentable and disappear the moment the user adds their own
how: Seed placeholder URLs deterministically from the slug; render placeholders only when the user's own field is empty; make the gallery a real add/remove editor

title: Machine-readable reusable-module hub for agents
detail: A dedicated repo + Worker hosting each dependency-free module in its own folder, indexed by a modules.json (raw file URLs, API, usage, deps) plus /llms.txt and /AGENTS.txt
why: Lets any coding agent discover and copy a module's full source in two requests, and makes adding a new module one folder + one JSON entry
how: public/<slug>/ per module; modules.json as the machine index; llms.txt/AGENTS.txt as the agent contract

title: Append-only field-change version history (old-new diffs)
detail: Every change to a project's info is archived append-only and shown as a readable old-to-new diff in an 'Activity & version history' panel, capturing edits from both the UI and the agent API
why: Gives a tamper-evident audit trail of who changed what and when, with no schema migration and nothing ever modifiable or deletable
how: Add an archiveEdit() helper that writes the field diff into the existing append-only logs table at both UPDATE sites (source: user vs claude-code); render as a diff log kind

title: Heirloom hand-down account (recovery key = ownership transfer)
detail: The whole account is designed to be handed to the child later as an 18th-birthday keepsake, made literally true because the cloud data is gated only by a portable recovery key
why: Turns a planner into a keepsake, a genuinely novel emotional moat no ad-funded incumbent offers
how: Keep all cloud data behind a single transferable recovery key (no email-locked account); surface 'one day, hand them the key' in-app

title: Loss-sensitive 'quiet pause' path (stop the cheerful nagging)
detail: A pause control that halts all weekly prompts/countdowns with an optional private note, shows 'the countdown is resting', and replays the note before resuming, plus a 'close this chapter quietly' option
why: Pregnancy/period apps are widely criticised for firing celebratory notifications after a loss; almost nobody designs the graceful exit
how: Add a pause state that suppresses time-based prompts, stores an optional user note, and offers a no-fanfare close; keep all data intact

title: Era-aware app that grows with the user
detail: One countdown that rolls itself from due-date to 1st/2nd/3rd birthday and re-labels content by era; setup offers 'expecting' vs 'baby already here' vs 'adopting/arrival day'
why: Extends product lifespan far beyond the ~9-month window competitors churn at, and serves adjacent segments
how: Drive labels and prompts off a computed life-stage rather than a single fixed mode; branch onboarding into the relevant era

title: Time-gated content reveal with an 'unlocks soon' teaser
detail: Only arrived weeks appear plus one locked teaser card ('unlocks Saturday - in 4 days')
why: Creates a weekly reason to return and an anticipation loop, rather than dumping all content up front
how: Compute each entry's unlock date from an anchor; render passed entries, hide future ones, show one next-up locked teaser with countdown

title: Server-enforced role-based share links (no accounts)
detail: Collaboration via copyable editor/viewer/admin links backed by worker share-tokens: viewers rejected server-side (403) on writes, only super-admin can grant admin or revoke, revoked links die instantly
why: Canva/Docs-style multi-user editing without forcing accounts, with authorization enforced on the server not the client
how: Mint role-scoped tokens in a Worker/KV; check role server-side on every mutating endpoint; keep recovery key only with owner

title: Personal photo as full-bleed wallpaper while themes keep the accents
detail: Users set their own photo as a 100%-cover background with an adjustable readability veil, while the theme still drives buttons/nav/accent colours on top
why: Deep personalization without sacrificing legibility or the design system
how: Fixed background-size:cover layer + themed veil slider; per-section override falling back to global photo; run every url() through a scheme-allowlist sanitizer

title: Self-building storybook timeline from a single anchor date
detail: A dashed spine that auto-generates dated chapters from one date, weaves the user's own photo-moments in chronologically, and floats a pulsing 'you are here' marker; reused across Ever After, Happy Travel, Hello Baby
why: Turns flat data into an emotional, anticipatory narrative and is highly reusable
how: Derive chapter dates from the anchor, mark past entries done and soften future ones, merge user moments by date, add a live position marker

title: Concentric closeness rings ('atom') for relationship maps
detail: Places the subject at centre and auto-orbits people onto rings by closeness, with rings fading outward, even spacing per ring, staggered spokes, and a legend
why: Communicates relationship closeness at a glance far better than a flat grid
how: Map each role to a ring radius, distribute members evenly with a per-ring angular offset so nobody stacks, dim guide circles with distance

title: One-time purchase over subscription for privacy-first products, with giftable unlock codes
detail: A single ~$29.99 unlock instead of a recurring fee, with Stripe promo codes, account-after-paying, and single-use gift codes so it can be gifted
why: A recurring charge contradicts a 'no ads, buy once, hand it down' privacy pitch and loses to churn on a short use arc; buy-once matches Etsy expectations and is giftable
how: Stripe Checkout -> webhook mints a single-use code -> redeem deep-link flips entitlement; lead the listing with 'Buy Once - No Subscription'

title: Data portability as verifiable trust proof
detail: One-tap 'Download everything (JSON)' export of the user's entire dataset
why: Makes a privacy/no-lock-in promise provable rather than merely claimed
how: Serialize all local/cloud state to a single downloadable JSON file from Settings

title: iOS-safe input spec: style :not([type]), 16px font, 44px target
detail: Add input:not([type]) so type-less boxes can't fall through to the default grey control, set 16px font on phones to stop iOS tap-to-zoom, enforce 44px min height per Apple HIG
why: Type-less inputs silently escaped every input[type=...] rule (a real 'unstyled box' bug), and sub-16px fields trigger auto-zoom on iOS
how: Include :not([type]) in the input rule set, bump font-size to 16px at mobile widths, apply min-height:44px, scope dense-view overrides explicitly

title: Security headers belong in _headers, not the Worker, for static assets
detail: On Cloudflare, static assets are served directly at the edge and bypass the Worker's fallback handler, so header injection written in the Worker never runs on asset responses.
why: Teams add CSP/security headers in the Worker, verify one JSON route, and ship — while every actual HTML/asset response still goes out bare.
how: Put security headers in a public/_headers file (or the assets config); verify with a GET on a real asset URL, not a HEAD on the API.

title: INP is now the most-failed Core Web Vital — break up long tasks
detail: INP (replacing FID) scores the worst interaction latency; 43% of sites fail the 200ms bar in 2026. Any task >50ms blocks the main thread and delays taps/clicks.
why: Heavy synchronous render/parse work on interaction makes the UI feel janky and now directly hurts search ranking.
how: Chunk long JS with await/yield (scheduler.yield or setTimeout), debounce/throttle scroll+resize, use passive listeners, move heavy compute to a Web Worker, avoid forced synchronous layout.

title: Six fixes clear 96% of accessibility failures
detail: Low-contrast text (83.9% of pages), missing alt text (53%), missing form labels (51%), empty links (46%), empty buttons (31%), and missing document lang (14%) account for 96% of detected WCAG errors.
why: These exclude real users (and drive ADA/EAA lawsuits) yet are all caught by free automated scanners — cheap, high-leverage wins.
how: Enforce 4.5:1 text contrast (3:1 large), alt on every meaningful image, a <label> for every input, text/aria-label on every link+button, and <html lang> set.

title: Write-in custom categories via datalist beat fixed dropdowns
detail: Replaced fixed <select> category pickers (subscription/asset/debt/bank/card) with <input list=...> datalists — suggestions plus free write-in.
why: Every user's real-world categories differ; a closed dropdown forces mislabeling into 'Other'.
how: One reusable datalist helper feeding an <input list>; keep the common suggestions, allow anything typed.

title: New users get a light scaffold, not seeded sample data
detail: Defaults ship as empty category templates (zero sample entries); a landing 'Try the demo' button and ?demo=1 load rich example data, with a one-tap 'Start fresh'.
why: Seeding fake entries into a real account makes users delete demo data before they can trust their own numbers.
how: Keep structural scaffolding in defaults; move all example rows into loadExample(); gate demo behind an explicit action.

title: Idempotency keys on every mutating / retryable endpoint
detail: Any POST that creates or charges (payments, inserts, sends) must accept a client-supplied idempotency key and no-op on replay, returning the original result.
why: AI codegen omits idempotency, so a retry, double-tap, or network re-send creates duplicate rows/charges/emails. Edge runtimes and clients retry more than devs expect.
how: Client generates a UUID per logical action; server stores it (D1 unique index or KV) with the response and returns the stored result on repeat. Combine with a unique DB constraint so even a race can't double-insert.

title: Verify AI-suggested dependencies before trusting them
detail: Treat every package name and API the model emits as unverified until checked against the real registry/docs; pin exact versions and commit a lockfile.
why: LLMs hallucinate package names (slopsquatting supply-chain risk) and deprecated/imaginary APIs. Auto-installing or calling them causes build breaks or runs an attacker's squatted package.
how: Before adding a dep: confirm the genuine repo, publisher, and download history; pin x.y.z not ^; keep a lockfile; prefer platform-native bindings (D1/KV/Workers AI). Cross-check unfamiliar SDK calls against current official docs, not the model's memory.

title: Store timestamps as UTC epoch, format only on display
detail: Persist instants as UTC (epoch ms or ISO-with-Z); convert to local wall-clock strictly at render time. Never parse bare 'YYYY-MM-DD' or call toISOString() on a locally-constructed Date to store it.
why: new Date('2026-08-16') parses as UTC midnight, and toISOString() on a local Date subtracts the offset — both shift the calendar day by one for anyone west of UTC, and DST transitions move stored times by an hour. A top recurring AI-codegen date bug.
how: Store Date.now()/UTC; build local dates with explicit y,m,d fields (month is 0-indexed) or a date lib in a fixed zone; format for the user with Intl.DateTimeFormat and the user's tz. Round-trip through UTC only.

title: Split static-asset routing from the SPA fallback (and auto-recover)
detail: Requests for hashed assets must 404 when missing — never fall through to index.html — and index.html must be served no-cache while assets are immutable-cached.
why: Serving index.html (200 text/html) for a missing .js chunk turns a routine deploy into a white-screen ChunkLoadError for users with the page already open or a stale service worker.
how: In the Worker, match asset extensions first and return the asset or a real 404; only unknown non-asset paths get the SPA shell. Set Cache-Control: no-cache on the HTML, immutable long max-age on hashed assets, and add a one-time hard-reload recovery on failed dynamic imports.

title: Budget edge-storage access: batch and chunk, never N+1 in a loop
detail: Treat every D1/KV/R2/fetch call as a metered subrequest with hard caps (100 bound params per D1 statement, per-invocation subrequest limit). Design writes and reads to stay well under them.
why: AI codegen writes per-row queries and giant multi-row inserts that pass on demo data and then hit 'too many SQL variables' or 'too many subrequests' under real volume — a silent scaling cliff.
how: Use db.batch([...]) in one transaction; keep (rows x cols) under 100 placeholders per statement and chunk beyond that; replace N+1 loops with a single JOIN or bulk read; cache repeated fetches; push large fan-out to Queues/Workflows.

title: Honest free tier — don't gate the core loop behind a surprise paywall minutes in
detail: Across thousands of 1-3 star reviews the #1 pattern is 'free that turns into a paywall': the listing leads with free, then locks the thing the user opened the app to do within minutes.
why: The lowest-rated apps rarely fail on idea — they fail because the way they ask for money doesn't match what users thought they agreed to. Bait-paywalls burn the goodwill you need for retention and reviews.
how: Let the core loop (log a habit, write an entry, track a stitch, build a budget) work for free indefinitely. Charge for depth/scale/convenience, never for the primary verb. State the free/paid line plainly on the first screen that hints at cost.

title: Deliver first value before asking users to sign up or pay
detail: Onboarding-abandonment and paywall complaints share a root: apps demand an account (or a card) before the user has felt anything work.
why: Time-to-value beats commitment-up-front. A user who has already created something real is far likelier to register to save it than one asked to commit to a stranger.
how: Allow a full first session anonymously with local persistence; prompt to create an account at the moment there's something worth saving ('sign up to keep this'), and defer any paywall until after a genuine aha. Migrate the local work into the new account on signup.

title: Grandfather existing users through price changes; announce increases in advance
detail: A one-time-purchase-to-subscription switch is the canonical resentment story — the app may still be good, but the change breaks the value calculation for people who already paid, and users rage at prices that quietly climb between renewals.
why: Silent or retroactive price hikes convert your most loyal, longest-paying users into your loudest detractors.
how: When you change pricing, grandfather current subscribers at their existing rate (or give a long honored window), announce any increase before it hits with a clear opt-out, and never let a renewal price rise without an explicit heads-up the user can act on.

title: Request ratings/reviews only after a genuine win — never at friction points
detail: Never prompt on first launch, during onboarding, after an error, or in the middle of a paywall. A frustrated user handed a rating prompt gives you the one-star you spend months digging out of.
why: Review timing determines review score more than product quality does at the margins; asking at a low-goodwill moment manufactures your own bad ratings.
how: Trigger the ask only after a detectable success moment (streak milestone, project completed, export finished), rate-limit it, and suppress it entirely for N days after any crash, failed payment, or support contact.

title: Per-item reminder scheduling, not one global notification time
detail: A top request for habit/tracker apps: different habits need different reminder times. Users want the water reminder hourly and the journaling reminder at 9pm — not both on one global schedule.
why: A single app-wide reminder time makes reminders useless for everything except one habit, so users disable notifications entirely and then churn from forgetting.
how: Attach an optional schedule to each trackable item (times of day, days of week, frequency), default to sensible per-type suggestions, and let the user mute one item's reminders without silencing the app.

title: Humane notifications — no guilt-trip copy, capped frequency, quiet by default
detail: Notifications have drifted from helpful nudges to emotional manipulation ('We miss you! Keep your streak alive'). Users report coming to hate apps that shame them; capping alerts to roughly 3/day reduced stress in research.
why: Guilt-based nudges spike short-term opens but drive long-term disengagement and 'this app makes me anxious' reviews — the opposite of intended habit formation.
how: Write encouraging, blame-free copy (never 'you failed'). Cap total notifications per day, ship granular per-category toggles, default anything non-essential to off, and offer quiet hours. Frame returns as welcome, not owed.

title: Keep sensitive personal data local or E2E-encrypted — no third-party ad/analytics SDKs on it
detail: Period/pregnancy apps became a privacy scandal: intimate cycle/pregnancy data leaked to ad platforms, and a 2025 jury held a major platform liable for collecting reproductive-health data via in-app trackers. Users mass-deleted trackers and demanded anonymous mode.
why: For pregnancy, baby, period, finance, and location data, a routine ad/analytics SDK turns your app into a liability that can expose users to real-world harm — and into a headline.
how: Classify health, reproductive, financial, and precise-location data as sensitive; keep it on-device or end-to-end encrypted; never route it through third-party ad/analytics/attribution SDKs; offer an explicit local-only/anonymous mode; and say plainly in-app what leaves the device.

title: Real 'delete my data' + a graceful-sunset export path
detail: Users learn that deleting the app does not undo data already collected/shared, and shutdown stories show apps switching off servers with no archive, no restore, no grace period — years of data gone.
why: A missing real-delete erodes trust the moment a privacy scare hits; a missing sunset plan turns an eventual wind-down into a betrayal. Both are trust primitives, not edge cases.
how: Provide a one-tap 'delete my account and data' that actually purges server records, backups, and third-party copies, and confirm honestly what it can and can't reach. Separately commit to a sunset policy: advance notice plus a full self-serve export before any shutdown.

title: Respect system font scaling / Dynamic Type — never cap text size
detail: Apps that ignore the device's font-size setting force low-vision and older users to pinch-zoom or leave; a large majority of surveyed users say accessibility barriers significantly hurt their mobile experience.
why: Fixed pixel type and hard-coded heights silently exclude a large share of real users (seniors, low vision, situational strain) and invite ADA-style complaints — while costing nothing to get right.
how: Size text in rem/relative units tied to the root, let containers grow with content, and test the whole UI at ~200% zoom / largest system font. No pixel-locked font sizes on body copy, and no clipping when text scales up.

title: Smoke-test the core user loop before every deploy
detail: 'An update that broke the core feature' is one of the universal 1-star patterns: the one thing people relied on stopped working and the next release didn't bring it back.
why: A regression in the primary verb (save an entry, log a habit, check out, count a stitch) churns your most engaged users instantly and floods reviews.
how: Keep a tiny checklist/automated smoke test of the core loop (sign in, create, edit, save/sync, reload-and-still-there, export) and run it against the built artifact before shipping. Never deploy a build where the core loop is red.

title: No-show protection: deposit or card-on-file with a fair policy
detail: Let owners require either a partial deposit (deducted from the final bill) or a card-on-file only charged on a late-cancel/no-show, paired with a plain cancellation policy shown before the client confirms.
why: No-shows are the top revenue leak for appointment businesses; salons/spas using deposits report large drops. Card-on-file is more palatable because clients don't part with money upfront but know there's a consequence.
how: Per-service toggle (deposit amount or card-hold), surface the policy on the confirm step, and support a gradual rollout (new clients and weekend slots first). Never auto-charge without showing the agreed policy.

title: Automated appointment reminders (24-48h before)
detail: Send an automatic reminder 24-48 hours ahead with a one-tap confirm/reschedule link, then optionally a shorter same-day nudge.
why: Automated reminders alone cut no-shows substantially — the highest-leverage, lowest-friction lever a booking tool has.
how: Schedule reminders on booking creation (email always, SMS/WhatsApp where a number exists), include reschedule and cancel links so a can't-make-it frees the slot, and let the owner edit timing and copy.

title: Buffer time between appointments
detail: Let owners set a configurable gap (travel, cleanup, notes) before/after each service so the next slot can't be booked back-to-back.
why: Back-to-back bookings with no breathing room cause cascading lateness and de-facto double-booking complaints; buffers are frequently demanded and absent from lightweight tools.
how: Per-service before/after buffer minutes, subtracted when computing open slots, enforced in the same server-side availability check that prevents conflicts.

title: Invoice aging + auto-chase + 'viewed' receipts
detail: Give every invoice a live status (draft/sent/viewed/due/overdue/paid), group outstanding ones into aging buckets, and send polite automatic reminders on a user-controlled schedule.
why: Most freelancers are owed money at any time and describe chasing as a nightmare; they lack a way to see what's paid, due, or lost in a client's inbox.
how: Track a viewed timestamp (hosted invoice link open), show an aging dashboard, and let users enable auto-reminders at due-date, +7, +14 days with editable wording.

title: Own-your-data: one-click complete export, no lock-in
detail: A single always-available 'export everything' producing a complete standard-format archive (JSON + CSVs) of every entity and its history, plus a documented import path back in.
why: Buyers increasingly test export before committing, and platforms that make leaving painful earn active rage. For a user-first product, trivially portable data is the honest differentiator.
how: Reuse the full object-graph export (contacts + notes + activity + attachments + finance), keep it free and self-serve, print row counts for verification, and state plainly in-app that users can leave any time.

title: Import/migration reconciliation report
detail: After any bulk import or migration, show a reconciliation summary — rows in, rows created, duplicates merged, rows skipped — with a downloadable list of every skipped row and the reason.
why: The defining pain of switching tools is silent loss; a visible count is what lets users trust the move.
how: Instrument the importer to emit counts and a per-row outcome, render them on a post-import screen, and offer 'download skipped rows'. Recommend keeping source data until counts reconcile.

title: Lean core by default, advanced features progressively revealed
detail: Ship the everyday jobs (add a contact, log a note, book, invoice) front-and-centre and tuck configuration, custom fields, automations and analytics behind an 'advanced' reveal.
why: Most small businesses use less than half their CRM's features and roughly a third abandon within a year over complexity — 'too complicated' is the #1 SMB churn reason. Simplicity is the retention feature.
how: Default new accounts to a minimal surface, gate power features behind a clearly labelled toggle/section, and let complexity grow only as the user reaches for it.

title: Prompt Etsy AI-content disclosure before publish
detail: When a listing uses AI-generated or AI-assisted images/text, surface a reminder to disclose it per Etsy's current policy, and offer ready disclosure wording.
why: Non-disclosure of AI-generated images is an active Etsy suspension trigger and appeals are frequently rejected — a compliance landmine an optimizer tool should defend against, not walk sellers into.
how: Detect/flag AI-origin assets in the listing draft, show a non-blocking compliance note with a copy-paste disclosure line, and link the current policy. Keep it advisory and honest — never assert Etsy rules that aren't published.

title: True net-profit-after-fees per listing
detail: Show the seller what they actually keep: subtract Etsy's stacked fees (listing fee, transaction % on item + shipping + gift wrap, payment processing, and the Offsite Ads fee where it applies) from the sale price, per listing.
why: Fee rage is a top Etsy complaint because the fees compound invisibly; sellers routinely misjudge margins. A clear net-take number is decision-grade information.
how: Add a fee-aware profit field to each listing/price suggestion using current rates, flag when a price barely clears fees, note that the Offsite Ads fee only hits attributed sales, and keep rates in one config so they stay current.

title: Test the whole UI at 200% zoom and the largest system font
detail: Size text in relative units tied to the root and let containers grow with content, then verify nothing clips or overlaps at 200% zoom and maximum system font size.
why: Pixel-locked type and fixed heights silently exclude seniors, low-vision and situationally-strained users — a large share of the audience for keepsake, baby, wedding and finance products.
how: rem/em for type and spacing, min-height instead of height, no overflow:hidden on text containers; add a zoom pass to the pre-ship checklist.

title: Verify, don't claim — every assertion needs a primary source
detail: Treat any factual statement shown to a user (a statistic, a market claim, a comparison, a compliance assurance) as unpublishable until it is traced to a primary source recorded alongside it.
why: AI-assisted copy makes confident, plausible, unverified assertions cheap to produce and expensive to retract; a single false 'first/only' claim damages trust more than the claim ever earned.
how: Keep a claims register mapping each user-facing claim to its source and date; re-check on a schedule; prefer provable framing over superlatives; delete anything you cannot cite.

title: Classify data sensitivity before choosing where it lives
detail: Decide up front which fields are sensitive (health, reproductive, financial, precise location, children's data) and let that classification dictate storage, transport and whether any third party may ever see it.
why: Retrofitting privacy is far harder than designing it, and the categories that cause real-world harm and regulatory action are knowable on day one.
how: Tag each field at schema-design time; route sensitive classes to local-only or end-to-end-encrypted storage; forbid them in logs, URLs and third-party SDKs by lint rule, not by memory.

title: Ship deletion and export on the same day as signup
detail: Build 'download everything' and 'delete everything' as part of the account feature itself, not as a later compliance task.
why: Both are legal rights and both are trust primitives users increasingly test before committing; adding them late means retrofitting across every table and blob store.
how: One export endpoint serialising the full object graph including media, and one delete path that purges records, backups and third-party copies — with honest disclosure of anything it cannot reach.

title: A core-loop smoke test is the highest-leverage test you can write
detail: One scripted pass through the primary verb — sign in, create, edit, save, reload and confirm persistence, export — run against the built artifact before every deploy.
why: 'An update broke the core feature' is one of the universal one-star patterns; users forgive missing features but not regressions in the thing they rely on.
how: Automate it against the deployed preview rather than a mock, and make a red result block the deploy even when the change looks unrelated.

title: Treat the share card as part of the product, not an afterthought
detail: Every shareable page gets a title, description and a 1200×630 og:image, verified in a card validator before launch.
why: Links are the primary distribution channel for a small product; a bare URL in a message or post converts far worse than a rendered preview with a title and image.
how: Add og:/twitter: tags to the page template so new pages inherit them, generate the image from the page's own design language, and validate after every deploy.

title: Make silent failure impossible by default
detail: No empty catches, a .catch on every chain, global error and unhandledrejection handlers, and a build stamp attached to every report.
why: The worst production bugs are the ones that generate no signal — a swallowed error looks identical to working software until a user complains weeks later.
how: Centralise error handling in one helper that always logs with context and always surfaces a user-visible state; lint against bare catch blocks; correlate every report to a deploy id.

title: Errors need a user-visible state, not just a log line
detail: Every failure path should render something honest to the user — a retry affordance or a plain explanation — in addition to being reported.
why: Logging alone leaves the user staring at a spinner or an unchanged screen, which reads as a broken product even when the failure was transient and recoverable.
how: Pair each catch with both a report and a UI state; prefer 'that didn't save — retry' over a silent revert, and never let a failed write look like a successful one.

title: Track deployed serverless/edge functions in the repo
detail: Serverless functions (Supabase edge functions, Cloudflare Workers/Pages Functions) that are deployed but not committed to the repo become invisible — an agent or teammate reads the repo, concludes the function is missing, and builds a redundant, contract-mismatched replacement.
why: A whole live payment/auth backend can be absent from source control; the next person duplicates it or routes around it, adding risk and drift. It cost a real detour on Finished. (a needless Cloudflare create-checkout in front of the working, deployed Supabase one).
how: Keep a tracked copy of every deployed function under supabase/functions/ or functions/, secrets read from a vault (never in the file), with a header noting it mirrors the live version. Diff repo-vs-deployed as part of review.

title: Embedded-view pattern: one component, standalone or nested
detail: A feature that has a full page (its own header + back button) often also wants to appear as a section inside a hub. Add an  prop that hides the component's own chrome so the host provides the back/title, and render the same body in both places.
why: Avoids a second implementation and keeps behaviour identical; lets a rich view (e.g. Follow-ups) live both as its own screen and as a tab inside another tool (Task Manager) with no double header.
how: Gate the header/back on !embedded; neutralise the standalone padding/max-width when embedded; pass onBack that returns to the host section. Verify no double header and that deep actions still work.

title: Strategy Lab: 'survives' is a multi-pillar rule that names the failing pillar, and thin samples show their trials but can never pass
detail: Replaced a 5-window/16-variant check with 200 Monte-Carlo reshuffles of the strategy's own trades, up to 40 rolling windows, a robustness sweep and a 10-symbol hold. A strategy earns paper trading only if every pillar clears (>=60% Monte-Carlo with positive median, >=55% windows, >=55% robustness plateau, >=half the symbols, positive out-of-sample) and it has >=15 trades; under that it still displays the trials but is flagged THIN and cannot pass.
why: A single lucky split or a short record can look like an edge; showing the trials makes fragility visible while the hard rule stops a flattering result being promoted, and naming the failing pillar tells the user what to rework.
how: Compute each pillar as a boolean, verdictPass = all pillars && !thin, build the failure sentence from the failed pillar names, guard below ~5 trades with 'not enough to judge', and validate the maths in a Node harness on real candles before shipping.

title: Translate every percentage into dollars at $50 / $5,000 / $500,000 and into 'winners out of every 100 trades'
detail: Hit rate is stated as 'about 22 winners out of every 100 trades' and each return (median, best-5%, worst-5%, whole record, average trade) is shown as +/- dollars for three account sizes with a liquidity caveat at size.
why: Percentages are abstract; a trader feels what -36% means at $5k, and the same framing keeps expectations honest for small accounts.
how: One shared helper pctToMoney(pct) over a MONEY_SIZES array plus a signed formatter that never prints '+-'; reuse it in the Lab and the track-record modal.

title: Prove client logic of a login-gated app with a Node harness of faithful copies run on real public data
detail: When the authed modal cannot be driven (no credentials, candles endpoint returns 401), copy the pure functions (backtester, Monte-Carlo, scan) into a .mjs harness, feed them real public market data with permissive CORS, then confirm on the live deploy that window.Views.x is a function (the IIFE ran), the console is clean and the new strings exist in the served bundle.
why: It verifies the maths and the bundle without ever typing a credential, and it catches guard-rule mistakes (a thin-sample rule that blocked the very trials the user wanted) before shipping.
how: Write the harness against exact copies, print per-pillar results, patch the rule, re-run, then render the real HTML templates from a localhost http.server for visual proof.

title: Make a product-policy rule executable: verdict stored per product, unknown categories fail closed, and the seed builder must refuse adversarial listings
detail: The 'no licence needed' promise lives in compliance.js (category rules, claim tripwires such as health claims on apparel or a power bank filed as decor) and is applied identically to seller listings, admin writes and AI-drafted listings; seed/build.mjs screens every SKU and also asserts a set of must-refuse items.
why: A rule in a PDF gets ignored by the first seller who uploads something else; a gate in code plus must-fail tests keeps the promise true after every change.
how: Single screenListing(category,title,description,evidence) returning allow/verdict/missing; fail closed on unknown categories; add adversarial fixtures to the seed script and fail the build loudly if one is admitted.

title: Show every applied filter as a removable chip, especially filters applied by voice or the URL
detail: A voice command navigated to /c/homedecor?max=5000 and the result list was correct, but the sidebar radios showed nothing selected, which reads as a broken filter. Browse now reads filters from URLSearchParams and renders a chip per active filter (query, price, verified, sort) that can be cleared.
why: A filter that is applied but invisible looks like a bug, and shared links must restore the same view.
how: Parse q/sort/min/max/verified/rating from location.search on route load, render chips in the results bar, and let each chip clear one param.

title: Switching a storefront's currency means converting at a verified FX rate with retail rounding and sweeping every default
detail: Relabelling GBP prices as USD would have silently cut every price about 26%. Rate was verified from two sources (1.3538), prices converted and rounded to .99, and price, compare_at, cost, wholesale tiers, free-shipping threshold, flat shipping, money() default, schema defaults, filter bands, schema.org priceCurrency and the voice parser's currency words were all moved together.
why: A partial swap leaves the catalogue in one currency and thresholds or defaults in another.
how: Script the conversion over every price-bearing column, grep for the old symbol/code, then verify with a server-side re-priced checkout in the new currency.

title: The Bash tool rejects commands containing raw control characters: write control-character regexes as \x00-\x1f escapes
detail: Pasting a regex that contained literal control bytes into a heredoc made the command fail validation ('control characters that would be hidden in the approval dialog'), and the Write tool silently dropped them from the file.
why: Retries wasted several turns and the written file was missing the character class.
how: Write /[\x00-\x1f\x7f]/ with backslash escapes via Write or a python chr(92) build, then node --check the file.

title: Verify a Vite + Pages deploy by hash parity with a local build, not by grepping for a marker in one chunk
detail: A marker grep for a new localStorage key found nothing in main-*.js and the lazy index-*.js chunks even though the commit had deployed; the code lived in styles-*.js. Running npm run build and comparing the content-hashed bundle names (main-CiaiF9mp.js, styles-BkZer-k7.js) with the live HTML proved the live build was byte-identical.
why: Chunk names are misleading and a negative grep can trigger a false 'not deployed' panic or an unnecessary redeploy.
how: Build locally, compare ls dist/assets with the asset paths in the live index.html, then spot-check strings across all referenced chunks with grep -F.

title: Seed profile-dependent UI synchronously from a last-known localStorage copy, and clear it on sign-out
detail: The home 'Your story' ring flashed the default silhouette on every load because the own profile came from an async Supabase call with only a 30 s in-memory cache. The profile is now persisted under finished.me, read synchronously to seed state, never blanked if the refresh returns null, and removed in signOut().
why: Removes the placeholder flash while preventing the next account on a shared device from inheriting the previous avatar.
how: cachedProfile() getter + setItem after each successful getProfile + removeItem in signOut; initialise useState from the cache and guard the refresh with a null check.

title: Before porting a feature into the module registry, check the registry, untracked dirs and git log for a sibling session building the same thing
detail: Two sessions ported overlapping modules the same day (to-do-list vs todo-list, day-planner vs routine-timetable, plus goals/goal-celebrate) and only discovered it from git status noise; the registry reached 20 entries with near-identical names.
why: Duplicate work and confusing near-identical slugs force the owner to reconcile later.
how: Run git status/log and list public/ and modules.json first, pick a distinct purpose and name, and write the intended slug into the board before building.

title: Check every pricing bullet's verb against what the feature itself disclaims before it ships
detail: A legal read of new tier bullets found one real exposure ('prove the ROI' vs the feature's 'direction not a perfect number'), two bullets that are only safe because an in-app caveat exists (photo-proof IP caveat and logo stripping; valuation shown as a range), and old absolutes ('no caps on anything', '$80-90/mo of separate tools') that need fair-use wording or a named basket on file.
why: Marketing absolutes create substantiation risk even when the product is honest.
how: For each bullet list the in-product caveat, replace absolute verbs (prove, guarantee, unlimited) with measurable ones (track, see the payback), and keep the caveat visible where the feature is used.

title: Blank screenshots and 30 s tool timeouts mean the Browser pane is hidden or the tab is not fronted, not that the page is broken
detail: Repeatedly the DOM and console were healthy while screenshots came back blank or timed out ('pane is not displayed', 'tab is not fronted'). Calling tabs_context and tabs_select on the tab restored painting; when the compositor stayed wedged, read_page, javascript_tool, console and curl proved the same facts.
why: It stops a false 'the app is broken' conclusion and avoids hacks like forcing .reveal elements visible.
how: Check tabs_context for 'hidden/not fronted', tabs_select the tab, retry once; otherwise verify through DOM/JS/console/network and state that visual proof was not possible.

title: Primary-source fetch ladder when WebFetch is blocked: Browser pane text, curl + pypdf for regulator PDFs, and record the rest as unverified
detail: A regulatory study hit domain-verification errors, 403s and bot checks on FinCEN, a law-journal article and a central-bank PDF. Reading them via the Browser pane get_page_text, downloading PDFs with curl -A and extracting with pypdf (pdftotext was absent) worked, while Reloadly's KYB list, Trustpilot and a World Bank page stayed unverifiable and were labelled as such.
why: Reports stay source-verified without guessing around blocked pages.
how: Try WebFetch, then navigate + get_page_text, then curl -A 'Mozilla/5.0' + pypdf, tag FACT/SIGNAL/HYPOTHESIS, and list unverified items explicitly.

title: Serialise iOS and macOS xcodebuild runs: parallel builds in one build directory collide
detail: Launching the iPhone and Mac builds at the same time in native/build produced a build collision; chaining them one after the other and auto-committing on green worked and let the session continue.
why: A collided build wastes minutes and can leave a half-written product.
how: Run 'xcodebuild ... iphonesimulator && xcodebuild ... macosx && git commit' in one background chain and poll the output file instead of sleeping.

title: Scanner detector for shadowed globals: duplicate window.X assignments and duplicate switch case labels across script files
detail: Add a shadowing family to the Bug Ledger scanner: (a) the same window.<name> = assigned in more than one script listed in index.html, reported in load order so the later wins is explicit; (b) duplicate case '<act>' labels inside one switch; (c) typeof X==='function' call sites where X has no definition anywhere.
why: Three Hallalu incidents (clientMeetingsCard defined in app.js and projects.js, a second case 'mark-sent', two onboarding flows) all passed node --check and rendered nothing wrong until a feature silently did not appear. The agent even believed clientMeetingsCard was undefined because its grep stopped at app.js and views.js.
how: Parse the script order from index.html, collect definitions per file with a regex, flag name collisions and orphan hooks; run it in scan.mjs --catalog and in the /finish checklist before any new window.* function is added.

title: Before building from a long prompt in a shared repo, diff against what other sessions just shipped
detail: Two sessions worked the same Hallalu repo within hours: one built the client-page Meetings widget (projects.js) and the mark-sent handler while another, answering a prompt that asked for the same thing, built a duplicate that was overridden at load time. A third check found the repo had moved eight commits (v263 to v271) while a session was paused.
why: Duplicate builds waste a wave and leave dead code that looks verified in source but never runs.
how: At the start of every wave run git fetch plus git log --since=3.days --stat -- public/, grep the repo for each function and action name about to be added, and re-sync again before shipping.

title: Give free-tier users a real AI recap and Ava through Workers AI instead of a hard paywall
detail: Ava's askAI() returned {error:'plan'} when needAI failed, and recaps fell to a verbatim on-device summary. A cheap flag now routes free users to @cf/meta/llama-3.3-70b-instruct-fp8-fast while Claude Haiku stays the premium voice, and Workers AI is the universal backup if the paid provider fails.
why: The recap is the product's best moment; showing a raw transcript there is the worst first impression, and Workers AI costs only Neurons.
how: aiText({cheap:true}) tries Workers AI first; the client always sends provider and cheap; the UI upsells 'sharper writing with Claude' rather than blocking the feature.

title: House shell helper for macOS: perl-alarm timeout plus a fresh Chrome profile per headless run
detail: macOS has no timeout command; three sessions hit it (Evertrue remote probe, Finished contact sheet, PostPlan slide export). The working helper is t(){ perl -e 'alarm shift; exec @ARGV' "$@"; } combined with a mktemp --user-data-dir for every headless Chrome call.
why: Without a hard limit a wedged render or a hung wrangler dev --remote probe consumes the 120s to 600s tool budget and gets moved to the background silently.
how: Put the helper and the per-run profile pattern in the sell and kindly skill snippets and in compose.mjs and shoot.mjs; always wrap network probes and Chrome launches.

title: pxb gen: retry transient flux-2-dev 502s and report per-job status in parallel runs
detail: Two of five parallel flux-2-dev bakes returned 502 'FLUX.2 dev could not bake that'. A shell pool using & printed 'done' while two files were missing, and manual retries ran past 300 seconds and were pushed to the background.
why: Silent partial batches cost credits and let a missing portrait ship unnoticed.
how: Add --retry N with backoff, a non-zero exit code on failure, and a pxb batch file.json --parallel 2 mode that prints id, status and cost per item; the CLI should also verify the output file exists and is not blank.

title: Marketing-from-URL: say so when the page is an empty JavaScript shell before drafting the brief
detail: On a client-rendered site the drafter saw about 1.8 KB of HTML and guessed grey colours and a corporate audience; the brand was corrected by hand through the briefs API before any credits were spent.
why: A wrong brief makes every concept off-brand and the user only finds out after paying for the bake.
how: If extracted text or product count is below a threshold, render the page in a browser fetch or show a banner 'I only saw N characters - check palette and audience' and require brief confirmation before the first paid bake.

title: paint-a-fix should show a before/after diff and warn when the masked region barely changed
detail: An sd15-inpaint fix on a third hand returned a success line and cost one credit, but the extra hand was still there; a flux-2-dev re-bake fixed the pose.
why: A fix that silently does nothing wastes credits and leaves a visible AI artefact in a shipped creative.
how: Compare pixels inside the rectangle before and after, warn below a change threshold, and offer a remove-object mode using a klein edit with the original as reference.

title: Portrait preset for realistic people: flux-2-dev, clean seamless backdrop and an equipment negative list
detail: flux-1-schnell portraits read as hand-drawn; flux-2-dev gave the realism, but backdrops showed light stands and the top edge of the paper. The recipe that worked: 'clean seamless soft neutral grey studio background, evenly lit, absolutely no photography equipment' plus a negative list (light stand, softbox, tripod, backdrop edge, backdrop seam, plastic skin), then a fault check of every PNG.
why: The user rejected the first sets as not looking like true professional photos; a baked-in preset avoids repeating the rework.
how: Ship it as a pxb preset (portrait-pro) with the negative list prefilled, flux-2-dev as default and a post-bake checklist (hands, props, equipment, edges).

title: Reports are append-only, so republishing creates a new id and the already-shared link keeps saying 'Not shipped yet'
detail: Republishing the report with a ship block (committed, deployed, version) produced a second report; the first, which the user had opened, still showed the stale status.
why: The link the user holds is the one they trust; a stale 'not shipped' chip undermines the evidence.
how: Add apz report --supersede <id> that stamps the old report with 'superseded by <new id>' (append-only note, no edit), or publish the report once after ship.

title: Write the board state file outside the repo: .aprizely.worklog.json keeps getting committed and pushed
detail: The per-project board file lives in the working directory. It was swept into a SkillSea commit, pushed to a brand-new private GitHub repo for Evertrue after a manual check that it held no token, and shows as modified in Hallalu after every board update.
why: It is machine state that dirties every git status, can leak titles to GitHub and collides when two sessions use the same folder.
how: Store it under ~/.aprizely/sessions/<hash of cwd>.json, or have apz start append it to .git/info/exclude.

title: Give icon containers a default SVG size so an unsized inline SVG can never fill its column
detail: The most repeated UI bug across apps: Abba's heart inside a modal heading, Evertrue icons inside .kicker and then inside label (two separate rules needed in one session), Pixelbake's robot icon in a definition list and the album picker, and Hallalu chart SVGs. Note that Hallalu's own global svg:not([width]) default shrank unsized chart SVGs to 16x16, so a blanket rule has a cost.
why: An unsized SVG expands to its container width and buries the real content, and it is invisible to node --check and unit tests.
how: Scope a default (width and height 1.1em) to icon contexts such as .kicker svg, label svg, h2 svg and dd svg, give charts explicit viewBox with width:100%, and add a scanner check for icon strings injected into elements without a size rule.

title: Always-on plain-English explainer for every backtest and scan result, computed from the user's own numbers
detail: The strategy bot showed jargon (out-of-sample, PF, max DD) and only a demo-only walkthrough. A computed panel now says, for example, that $10,000 became $16,257 (+62.57%) but buy-and-hold made +92.15%, that out-of-sample profit is the real test, and what to do next, with a one-line gloss on every term plus an Ask Ava to go deeper button using Cloudflare AI; the whole-watchlist opportunity scan and the explainer were ported to native in tandem.
why: A beginner needs to know what a result means and what is only luck (22 variants tried, small sample) without leaving the screen.
how: Generate the explanation from the metrics with templates and real-world analogies (no model call needed), keep an LLM deep-dive optional, and test both web and native from the same wording table.

title: State the real limit when a laptop starts a phone call: web pages cannot hear a Continuity call
detail: Start call now fires a tel: link (rings through the paired iPhone on a Mac), but no browser can tap the audio of a Continuity or phone call; Hallalu transcribes through the laptop microphone, so putting the call on speaker is the only way both sides are heard.
why: The user said 'if it can't work with recording and transcript, don't'; claiming a transcript that cannot exist would be an invented capability.
how: Keep the dial action, show a one-line speaker tip beside the recorder, and state the limit in the help text.

title: Trace each prompt clause to evidence and name ambiguous clauses before building
detail: 'Link multiple clients to the same company' was built as multiple contacts and a main number inside one record, an audit then reported 'every request is implemented', and only a closer read exposed that grouping separate lead records under one company (companies.js) was missing. The same session wrote 'board finished' next to an open question.
why: An ambiguous clause interpreted narrowly produces a finished-looking board with a real gap, and the user loses trust in the word done.
how: Restate each ambiguous clause with the chosen interpretation (or build the broader reading), keep a clause table with file:line and an Open column, and lead the final message with an explicit Done versus Still-open split.

title: Catalog drifts from the skills it lists: edits need a manual node scan.mjs and wrangler deploy
detail: Changing the /finish skill description only reached skillsea.coconvo.workers.dev after running the additive scan (which also picked up a new patentscan skill) and a deploy; the repo has no git remote, so the commit could not be pushed.
why: A catalog that lags the skills undermines it as the single place to see what exists.
how: Run the scan from a post-edit hook or a scheduled task, deploy only when the diff is non-empty, and give the repo a private remote.

title: One goal system, three plain-English homes: daily goal leads Home, monthly goal on Money, challenge copy in words
detail: Goal meant a Studio listing challenge, a Routine item, a dashboard profit goal and a Money goal. The new layout leads Home with Today's goal (progress and an I hit it confirm, modelled on Hallalu), puts a monthly-goal card with profit, revenue and orders on Money, links Money and Budget both ways, renames Routine to To Do Checklist, and rewrites the Studio modal to 'New listings to publish in October 2026'.
why: The user could not tell what to type into the goal and challenge fields, and a goal they set did not appear where they looked.
how: Name the three horizons once (today, month, challenge), show each in one place, and make every goal field state its unit and month in words.

title: Reusable theme modules need an explicit token map and escape-hatch tokens
detail: abba-backgrounds uses --txt, --dim and --bg2 while Hallalu uses --ink, --ink-2 and --bg-soft, so a THEME_MAP had to be written; the sidebar background was a hard-coded gradient so a --side-bg token with a fallback was needed; and the ThemeStudio preset click kept fine-tune overrides (patched in the module and redeployed).
why: Each consumer re-solves the mapping, and presets that do not reset overrides never give the user the full preset.
how: Ship maps/<vocabulary>.json with the module, document that every themed surface reads var(--x, fallback), make presets reset overrides, and expose --side-bg and --side-ink as standard parts.

title: For developer-tool marketing weight sets toward real product screens and disclose AI photos
detail: Evidence gathered for the Aprizely creative run said builders trust real product screens more than AI-generated faces, so the 14-piece set was weighted toward real screens, composed with a real-product-screen layout, and AI photos carry an on-image disclosure line ('AI-generated photo - real product').
why: Trust in AI-generated imagery is mixed and an undisclosed AI face risks the credibility the product is selling.
how: In the sell playbook add a real-screen ratio per set, a disclosure line on any AI photo, and a QA item that checks the disclosure is legible at feed size.

title: Syntax-gate every deploy: node --check all edited JS, and again after any killed or partial agent run
detail: A dashboard edit left a duplicated half-open if(photo){ block in wed.js, producing 'Unexpected end of input' at line 367 that would have blanked the whole wedding app; node --check found it before deploy. In a later session node --check over ~30 files edited by agents killed mid-run proved no partial edit shipped.
